obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 as a service provider: Payment Processing
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (PCI SSC, June 2024); card brand and sponsor agreement terms
basis: The division stores, processes and transmits cardholder data for about 920,000 merchants (about 29 billion transactions a year), above Visa's 300,000-transaction threshold for a Level 1 service provider. The 2025 ROC and AOC (Compliant, 2026-01-22) were issued by a QSA. PCI DSS has no size exemption

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 as a service provider: Payments Software Platform
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 for hosted storefront pages
basis: The gateway transmits cardholder data to seven processors and holds its own ROC and AOC (2026-03-31); the division hosts about 180,000 storefront pages that embed payment fields, a service that can affect the security of merchants' cardholder data

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 as a service provider: Merchant Consulting
basis: Dispute services receive and handle account data in dispute evidence for about 2,100 merchants; for group merchants the work happens inside the processor's CDE (SYS-P6), and 620 clients do not process with the group

obligation: PCI PIN Security Requirements: Payment Processing
basis: PIN debit is processed through PIN translation in the payment HSMs; the PIN assessment is separate and outside this library

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Payment Processing
basis: A financial institution: data processing and transmission of financial data is a listed activity (225.28(b)(14)), and card processing is the whole business. No group entity is a bank or supervised by a federal banking agency, so no other regulator enforces safeguards under GLBA section 505 (314.1(b)). The rule covers cardholders' information that the division holds for other institutions (314.1(b)); the vault's size rules out the 314.6 exception

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Payments Software Platform
basis: Its gateway transmits payment transaction data for about 410,000 merchants and 1,900 ISVs (225.28(b)(14)); covered by the group program

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Merchant Consulting
applies: No (not a financial institution); a service provider to the processor
basis: Advisory, integration, PCI readiness and dispute services are not listed financial activities, so the division is not significantly engaged in financial activities (314.2(h)(3)(iv)). It receives customer information as a service provider (314.2(r)) to the Payment Processing division for dispute services, so the processor must oversee it and bind it by contract (314.4(f)). Group legal recorded the decision on 2026-06-12

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Qualified Individual employed by an affiliate
basis: The Group CISO, employed by the holding company, was designated in writing in 2025-06 as Qualified Individual for both financial-institution divisions; the last written report to the board risk committee is dated 2025-12-10

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Payment Processing
citation: 12 CFR 53.4 (Banks A and B); 12 CFR 225.303 (Bank C); 12 CFR 304.24 (Bank D)
basis: Each sponsor agreement states that clearing, settlement, reconciliation and merchant funding file services are performed for the bank and are subject to examination under 12 U.S.C. 1867(c). These are covered services (53.2(b)(5)), so the division is a bank service provider to each bank under the rule of that bank's regulator

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Payments Software Platform
basis: The division's service agreements list no covered services for any bank

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Merchant Consulting
basis: The division performs no services for any bank; its dispute work is for merchants and the processor

obligation: Computer-security incident notification by a banking organization: group
basis: No group entity is a bank or a bank holding company; the sponsor banks' own 36-hour notices to their regulators are the banks' duties, informed by the division's notice

obligation: Bank Service Company Act: Payment Processing
basis: Covered services named in all four sponsor agreements, with examination cooperation clauses; supported the 2025 OCC service provider examination

obligation: Interagency Guidelines: Payment Processing
applies: No (directly); applies through the sponsor agreements
basis: The Guidelines bind the sponsor banks; they reach the division through the sponsor agreements' service provider terms, tested in each bank's annual due diligence

obligation: Interagency Guidelines: Payments Software Platform, Merchant Consulting and group
basis: No group entity is a bank or a bank holding company, and neither division serves a bank

obligation: NCUA cyber incident reporting: all divisions
basis: No group entity is a federally insured credit union

obligation: SEC Regulation SCI: all divisions
basis: No group entity is an SCI entity (no exchange, clearing agency, ATS or plan processor)

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation: all divisions
basis: No group entity holds a New York banking, insurance or financial services license, registration or charter, so the 500.19(a) exemption analysis is not reached

obligation: CIRCIA: all divisions
basis: Proposed rule only (89 FR 23644); no final rule as of 2026-09-25; tracked on the group regulatory watch list

obligation: Card brand rules (Visa What To Do If Compromised and each brand's rules through the sponsor banks): Payment Processing
basis: The division stores, processes and transmits account data under the sponsor banks' memberships and is registered with the card brands

obligation: Card brand rules: Payments Software Platform gateway
basis: The gateway transmits account data to seven processors

obligation: Sponsor agreement notice clause: Payment Processing
basis: Notice to each sponsor bank of any suspected account data compromise within 24 hours

obligation: Intercompany agreements: gateway services (2023) and consulting dispute services (2025)
basis: Neither agreement has a PCI DSS responsibility matrix; the 2025 agreement has no safeguards clause

obligation: Standard ISV agreement (2025): Payments Software Platform
basis: Notice within 24 hours of an incident affecting ISV credentials or ISV data

obligation: Software terms of service and enterprise merchant contracts
basis: Notice to merchants without undue delay; 48-hour notice for 140 enterprise merchants; 99.9% monthly availability

obligation: Merchant agreements: Payment Processing
basis: 99.95% monthly availability for authorization; acknowledgment of the processor's responsibility for account data (PCI DSS 12.9.1)

obligation: Consulting engagement letters: Merchant Consulting
basis: Notice to clients within 72 hours of a confirmed incident affecting client data; confidentiality of client data

obligation: SOC 2 Type 2 commitments: Payments Software Platform
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; customer contracts
basis: Merchants and ISVs rely on the annual SOC 2 Type 2 report (Security, Availability, Confidentiality) for the 12 months ending September 30, last issued 2025-12-12

obligation: SOC 1 Type 2 and requested SOC 2: Payment Processing
citation: AICPA SOC 1; Trust Services Criteria; sponsor bank requests
basis: Annual SOC 1 Type 2 for the 12 months ending September 30; the sponsor banks' 2026 due diligence requests ask for a SOC 2 covering security, availability and processing integrity

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Payment Processing
basis: A for-profit company in commerce and not a bank, so outside the 45(a)(2) carve-out

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Payments Software Platform
basis: A for-profit company in commerce; marketing describes storefront checkout and the assistant's data handling

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Merchant Consulting
basis: A for-profit company in commerce; marketing promises bank-grade security

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: holding company
basis: The holding company is not a bank

obligation: COPPA Rule: Payments Software Platform (and all divisions)
basis: No child-directed service and no actual knowledge of child users; services are sold to merchants and ISVs

obligation: CCPA and CPPA regulations: Payment Processing
applies: Exempt at the data level for GLBA data
basis: Cardholder data held by the division is GLBA customer information

obligation: CCPA and CPPA regulations: Payments Software Platform
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.140(d); Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7120-7124
basis: Group revenue is above the CCPA revenue threshold; merchants' customers' data is not GLBA data; no written decision on the cybersecurity audit, risk assessment and ADMT duties

obligation: CCPA and CPPA regulations: Merchant Consulting
basis: Client contact data is personal information outside GLBA; covered by the same review as the Software division

obligation: DOJ Data Security Program: all divisions
basis: The group holds bulk personal financial data (about 640 million unique PANs in the vault; merchants' customer data in SYS-S1); vendor and app developer screening checks sanctions, not covered persons

obligation: Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act: Payments Software Platform
basis: The data use policy states that the division does not sell or transfer personal data to third parties for value, so it is not a data broker

obligation: FCC CPNI rules: all divisions
basis: No group entity is a telecommunications carrier or interconnected VoIP provider

obligation: FedRAMP: all divisions
basis: No federal agency customers

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure: group
basis: The holding company is a publicly traded SEC registrant; divisions send incident facts to the disclosure committee

obligation: IRC 7216 and IRS Publication 4557: Merchant Consulting
basis: The division prepares no tax returns

obligation: FAR 52.204-21 and DFARS 252.204-7012 with CMMC: all divisions
basis: The contract register lists no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: HIPAA as a business associate: all divisions
basis: Engagement letters exclude PHI, and no division handles PHI for a covered entity

obligation: Florida Bar Rules 4-1.1 and 4-1.6(e); AICPA Code ET 1.700: Merchant Consulting
citation: Rules Regulating The Florida Bar, Chapter 4; AICPA Code
basis: The division is neither a law firm nor a CPA firm and performs no legal or attestation work

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (automated decision-making technology): Payment Processing
basis: Effective 2027-01-01. The fraud model declines purchases automatically and the underwriting model scores merchant applications, many from sole proprietors; whether either is a consequential decision is under review

obligation: Colorado SB26-189: Payments Software Platform
basis: The merchant insights assistant answers merchants' questions about their own data and makes no consequential decision about a consumer

obligation: Colorado SB26-189: Merchant Consulting
basis: The division's only AI use case is staff use of generative AI for drafting (AI-007), which makes no consequential decision about a consumer

obligation: ECOA and Regulation B: Payment Processing
applies: Under counsel review (underwriting model); No (fraud model)
basis: Whether a merchant processing agreement is credit is under review for the underwriting model; the fraud model makes no credit decision, since issuers decide credit authorizations

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification): all divisions
basis: For cardholder data the divisions act as their merchants' or clients' third-party agent (501.171(6)); the processor holds merchant owner personal information as a covered entity. Other states' laws apply where affected individuals reside; Florida is the worked example

obligation: Money transmission licensing: Payment Processing
basis: Merchant funds settle through the sponsor banks' accounts; licensing is outside this security library
